caption:
ChatGPT users say their accounts were shut off on November 7 with no warning email.
Free API, team and even $200 a month Pro accounts were hit, and some lost years of chats and saved memories.
OpenAI has not explained the bans or said how many people were affected.

Do you keep a backup of your ChatGPT chats?

paragraphs.text: ChatGPT users began reporting on November 7, 2026 that their OpenAI accounts had been shut off without notice. When they tried to log in, they were shown a message saying the account had been deleted or deactivated, according to reports compiled by TokenPost and by MarsBit, published on KuCoin News.

Most of the affected users said they received no email warning before losing access. The reports did not include a count of how many accounts were affected, and OpenAI had not published an explanation as of November 9, according to PANews.

The deactivations reached several kinds of accounts, the reports said: free API accounts, shared team accounts and Pro subscriptions that cost $200 a month. One user said a Pro account that had been in use for five years was deactivated with no warning, according to TokenPost.

For some users, the loss went beyond the chatbot itself. A developer said years of conversation history and personal memories stored in the cloud could no longer be reached after the shutdown, TokenPost and MarsBit reported.

Ukrainian tech outlet dev.ua described the case of a Pro subscriber who raised the problem on OpenAI's community forum. He said an account_deactivated error appeared instead of the normal login, that he used the account only himself and that he protected it with a physical security key. He suggested the block might be linked to connecting to ChatGPT and Codex through VPN servers in different countries.

According to PANews, which cited reporting by Zhitong Finance and complaints on Reddit and in Chinese developer communities, users believe the bans came from automated, large scale detection on OpenAI's side rather than a review of each account. Some said they had followed the rules but were flagged because the system linked them to accounts that had already been banned.

PANews listed the groups that appeared to be hit hardest: subscriptions bought in low price regions, accounts registered in bulk, accounts that share a payment card or a device, accounts reached through relay or reverse proxy services, accounts tied to the resale of API quota and accounts suspected of model distillation. The outlet noted that OpenAI has carried out similar sweeps before, going back to 2023.

dev.ua also pointed to earlier limits set by OpenAI on how many paid ChatGPT accounts can be used on one device and how many subscriptions can be paid with one bank card, which can cost users access to some accounts even after they pay.
Appeals as the only route back

In the forum case reported by dev.ua, an OpenAI support representative told the user to file an appeal and said such cases are not discussed on a public forum. No specific reason for the block was given. Other users said their appeals were rejected quickly, the outlet reported.

The episode shows how much personal and work material now sits inside a single chatbot account. When access depends on an automated system that gives no reason and no warning, users who keep long project histories or saved memories in ChatGPT have little control over whether that material stays available, and the appeal process is the only visible path to recover it.
The next signal is whether OpenAI explains the criteria behind the November 7 deactivations or restores accounts that users say were flagged in error.
